- Forum quotes give the poster's username as displayed and the post date.

## Prior art and community discussion

**[1]** astroneer3141 et al. "A device to sense and prevent mount collisions?" *Cloudy Nights*, ATM, Optics and DIY forum, thread started 2025-12-18, page 1.
<https://www.cloudynights.com/forums/topic/987869-a-device-to-sense-and-prevent-mount-collisions/>
**Tier:** 4 (via reader)
Remote imager asks how others handle collision risk; proposes an IMU sensor on the OTA. Bob4BVM (2025-12-18): "Real protection is done with proper sensors set up to detect collisions, etc, and if triggered, they'd trip a control ckt which disconnects power from the prime mover (ie motor).. All easily done with a sensonr(s) on the moving part to detect collision and a contactor to break the power to motor." iluxo (2025-12-19): started an Arduino-accelerometer build that "opens a relay and kills the power to the mount" when in a no-go zone; training the no-go zone "opened a whole can of worms", an ASIAIR meridian flip stops "approx 5 millimeters" from the tripod so "to avoid unecessary 'emergency stops' it has to pretty accurate", and "Family life is busy at the moment so I shelved it". momo-chan (2025-12-19): "Does it power off the mount, or just stop? Recovery methods would also be necessary." ButterFly: a sensor only detects trouble where the sensor is. astroneer3141: magnet-reed switches "work only for a particular DEC angle". Bob4BVM, citing a professional safety-systems background: "we never, ever, trusted software as the final arbiter for safety decisions/control". Bob4BVM #18: contactor control "ALL outside of any software/uP-driven systems... you want it to fail in a safe mode"; sensors "can be fixed to pier". whereIsIt #20 on MPU-6050 accelerometers: "I certainly would Not use it if failure was important." (Page 1 also confirmed from an operator-supplied PDF, 2026-10-06.)

**[2]** Same thread, page 2 (posts 2025-12-20 to 2025-12-30).
<https://www.cloudynights.com/forums/topic/987869-a-device-to-sense-and-prevent-mount-collisions/page/2/>
**Tier:** 4 (via reader)
walt r: monitor motor current and "if current exceeds a set point, trip the 'fail-safe'". Bob4BVM: with large gear ratios "i'm not sure you'd see enough current change"; software hard stops are "a total violation of the fail-safe concept". 3C286: research radio telescopes used micro-switch "hard limit switches" with "pushers"; "I think the microswitches were push-to-break and if any of them were pushed, it tripped the drive controller at the HW-level. If any of the hard limit switches were tripped, it needed to be manually driven out of limits by someone at the telescope." Hierarchy: "1. Mechanical [best] 2. Electrical/Electronic 3. Software [worst]". Prefers microswitches over Hall/reed. Tony_Gondola-x: on an EQ6R the RA clutch slips first. brebisson: motor current cutoff "most likely the most fool proof system". whereIsIt: 3D printers "All use Micro/other Mechanical/Limit switches to Cause Stopping All 'further' Action."

**[3]** "Limit Switches for Astro-Physics AP1200." *kor-astro.net*, n.d.
<https://www.kor-astro.net/detail/limit_switch/ap1200_limit_switches.html>
**Tier:** 3
Arduino + MMA8451 accelerometer computes RA roll angle; "A normally open relay interrupts the power to the mount... If the angle goes out of those limits, the Arduino opens the relay, removing power from the mount. Manual recovery is necessary." Recovery: hold button 2 s, slew east within first 5 s. Limitation: single limit per direction regardless of declination. Motivation: "I want a simple and reliable failsafe."

**Tier:** 3

## Strain wave gear engineering and robot-joint analogues

**[54]** Kazerooni, H.; Ellis, S. "Dynamics and Control of Instrumented Harmonic Drives." *J. Dyn. Sys., Meas., Control* 117, 1995. NASA NTRS record 20040089424 (abstract only).
<https://ntrs.nasa.gov/search.jsp?R=20040089424>
**Tier:** 1 (abstract only; DOI 10.1115/1.2798517 failed to fetch)
"A high ratio harmonic drive is non-backdrivable because its output shaft cannot be turned by applying a torque on it."

**[55]** Nabtesco. "Backdrive capability in gearboxes: everything you need to know." 2026.
<https://www.nabtesco.de/en/the-company/news-detail/backdrive-capability-in-gearboxes-everything-you-need-to-know>
**Tier:** 2 (gear manufacturer)
"Strain wave gears and cycloidal gears are fundamentally reversible—when reversing, only the friction needs to be overcome." "complete self-locking cannot be guaranteed."

## Safety standards and industrial practice

**[68]** ISO. "ISO 13850:2015 Safety of machinery — Emergency stop function — Principles for design." Preview sample (iTeh).
<https://cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/59970/06ad76004ab746ff90b82cf44a8b0752/ISO-13850-2015.pdf>
**Tier:** 1 (sample ends at §4.1.1.6)
§4.1.1.2: "it shall be maintained until it is manually reset"; "it shall not be possible for any start command to be effective"; "The reset shall not initiate machine start up." §4.1.1.3: "complementary protective measure". §4.1.1.4: may need "braking devices" kept operational. §4.1.1.5: stop "without creating additional hazards". §3.1: E-stop "initiated by a single human action".

**[69]** ISO. "ISO 13850:2015" catalogue page.
<https://www.iso.org/standard/59970.html>
**Tier:** 1 (via reader)
Standard status "To be revised"; ISO/AWI 13850 under development.

**[70]** Pilz. "FAQ: Resetting the emergency stop." Article 180045, n.d.
<https://www.pilz.com/en-INT/support/faq/standards/articles/180045>
**Tier:** 3 (via reader; vendor)
"the emergency stop may only be reset directly on the emergency stop device on which the command was initiated and by intentional human action."

**[71]** Nix, D. "ISO 13850 Emergency Stop Requirements." *Machinery Safety 101*, 2026-05-18.
<https://machinerysafety101.com/2026/05/18/iso-13850-emergency-stop-requirements/>
**Tier:** 3
"The emergency stop command must be maintained until manually reset, and resetting the emergency stop function must not restart the machine on its own". Minimum reliability Performance Level c (ISO 13849-1); "single-channel architectures can achieve the required Performance Level with suitable component selection."

**[72]** Nix, D. "Understanding Safety Functions: Manual Reset." *Machinery Safety 101*, 2021-05-19.
<https://machinerysafety101.com/2021/05/19/understanding-safety-functions-manual-reset/>
**Tier:** 3
Disengaging the E-stop device is the manual reset; reset "shall not restart the machinery but only permit restarting" (quoting IEC 60204-1).

**[73]** Engineering Shield. "Designing E-STOP circuits to ISO 13850: manual vs auto reset." 2026-07-06.
<https://eshield.pl/en/knowledge/designing-e-stop-circuits-iso-13850-manual-vs-auto-reset/>
**Tier:** 3
Release, reset and start are separate steps; "The mere fact that the cycle does not restart automatically is not sufficient."

**[74]** Schneider Electric. "What are the stop categories?" FAQ FA122781.
<https://www.se.com/us/en/faqs/FA122781/>
**Tier:** 3
"Category 0: stopping by immediate cutting off of power to the actuators ( example: uncontrolled stop)."

**[75]** GT Engineering. "Stop functions." 2023-04-18.
<https://www.gt-engineering.it/en/insights/machinery-safety/stop-functions/>
**Tier:** 3
"Machines with moving parts without inertia and whose stop does not cause additional risks require stop in Category 0." For machines with inertia, "stop in Category 1 is required". Category 0 E-stop "is equivalent to the STO (Safe Torque Off) function".

**[76]** Bernstein. "What does positive opening mean?" n.d.
<https://www.bernstein.eu/en/service/bernstein-wiki/what-does-positive-opening-mean>
**Tier:** 3
Contact separation "must not depend on components such as springs"; welding risk from inrush and inductive loads.

<https://prod-edam.honeywell.com/content/dam/honeywell-edam/sps/siot/ja/products/switches/limit-switches/common/documents/sps-siot-app-note-limit-switches-positive-contacts-002427-3-en-ciid-179602.pdf>

There is a magnet on each side of the mount so it cannot go more than about 10 degrees passed horizontal in either direction. Just tested it and it works well." "if the mount gets 'lost' then it just keeps going. There are no physical stops... the GEMS just object and stop. The harmonic mounts just keep going. At least now this is not possible as the mount gets turned off." 2025-09-26: "I have added a wiring diagram of my solution to the DIY astronomer section" (not reached). gorann (2025-09-24): "I should install a micro switch... on the pier through which I would run the 12V to the mount. That would break the power to the mount when the scope gets close and touches the lever on the switch." Not reported as built. Reset not described.
